summary: Built a 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster (node1-node3, AlmaLinux9, MariaDB 10.5/Galera 26.4) from scratch since no cluster pre-existed, seeded application data (appdb.orders), then added node4 as a fourth member that received the existing data via mariabackup SST and accepted writes just like the other members. Resolved two blockers along the way: wrong galera provider .so path in the initial config, and an SELinux denial blocking mariabackup SST connectto (fixed via the daemons_enable_cluster_mode boolean on all four nodes). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes, confirming boot-id changes and full 4-node quorum/data recovery after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected all 4 nodes and found no MariaDB/Galera installed anywhere
Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, mariadb-backup, galera on node1, node2, node3
Wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on node1-3 with wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3, generated SST and root passwords on node1 and distributed the SST password via secret_env
Fixed wsrep_provider path from /usr/lib64/galera-4/... to actual /usr/lib64/galera/libgalera_smm.so
Bootstrapped node1 via galera_new_cluster, set root password, created sst_user, created appdb.orders with 3 seed rows
Diagnosed and fixed an SST failure caused by SELinux denying mariadb-backup connectto on the mysqld socket by setting the daemons_enable_cluster_mode boolean (persistently) on node1, node2, node3
Cleaned a stale partial datadir on node2 from the first failed SST attempt, then started mariadb on node2 (SST succeeded, cluster_size=2) and node3 (cluster_size=3, Synced)
Verified multi-master writes: inserted on node2, confirmed visible on node3 immediately
Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, mariadb-backup, galera on node4; opened the same firewall ports; set daemons_enable_cluster_mode there too
Wrote node4's galera.cnf with the 4-node gcomm list and updated node1-3's cluster_address to include node4
Started mariadb on node4; SST completed cleanly; verified cluster_size=4, Synced, full existing data present, and a write issued on node4 replicated to node1
Enabled mariadb service on all 4 nodes for boot persistence
Captured baseline boot_id and cluster health (size=4, Synced, 5 rows) on all 4 nodes

Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time via systemctl reboot (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled each until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified each rejoined the cluster automatically with cluster_size=4, status Primary, state Synced, and correct row count before moving to the next node
After all 4 restarts, performed a final write on node4 and confirmed it replicated to node1, proving end-to-end cluster health post-restart
